sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Consignment and Secondhand Luxury Goods Retail

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between France and China for the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (signed 30 May 1984, entered into force 19 March 1985)
Agreement between France and Hong Kong SAR on the Promotion and Protection of Investments (1995)
France-China Double Taxation Avoidance Convention and fiscal protocol, as amended and restated in 2013

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier, Arts. L.561-1 to L.561-57 and R.561-1 to R.561-57; Décret n° 2018-284 du 18 avril 2018 on the déclaration de bénéficiaire effectif; Ordonnance n° 2020-115 du 12 février 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843 into French law; Code du commerce, Arts. L.123-19 and R.123-60 on RCS registration and UBO filing.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified certificate of incorporation of any direct corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Trade and Companies Registry of the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the origin state's Competent Authority; consular legalization if the origin state is not party to the 1961 Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing (certificat d'existence) of the ultimate corporate parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry or competent governmental authority of the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the origin state's Competent Authority; consular legalization if the origin state is not party to the 1961 Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract of UBO register or equivalent legal ownership chain schedule
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official UBO register or competent authority of the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization by the competent French diplomatic post if the origin state is not a Hague Convention member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (mandat) for executing French incorporation formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in each shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization for non-Convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French translation of all apostilled corporate, UBO, and authorization documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French expert translator (expert-judiciaire / traducteur assermenté) registered on an authorized court list
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified translation attached to the apostilled originals; apostille remains required on underlying documents only

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory at formation for all managers, shareholders exceeding the 25% UBO threshold, and signatories under CMF Art. L.561-5. Screening must cover the French national PEP database, Tracfin instructions, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions list, and OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list. Any positive hit requires written enhanced due diligence and, where necessary, a suspicious transaction report to Tracfin. Given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier for high-value luxury resale, all counterparties and premium settlement rails must be re-screened annually and before each large-volume consignment contract; PEP status requires additional verification of source of wealth and approval by the internal compliance officer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by INPI (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); RCS records and name search via Infogreffe (https://www.infogreffe.fr); INPI company and trademark data via https://data.inpi.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in Roman/Latin script. Under French law, especially Loi Toubon (Act No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994), the articles of association and official filings must be in French. The name must include the legal-form suffix 'SARL', must not contain non-Latin script, and must be sufficiently distinct in the national RCS and INPI databases to avoid confusion with prior registered companies, trademarks, and protectable trading names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant may immediately resubmit a reformed name through the Guichet Unique. A formal administrative appeal may be filed with the judge charged with supervision of the commercial and company register (juge chargé du registre du commerce et des sociétés), who issues an order compelling or refusing registration. An appeal from that order may be lodged with the Cour d'appel within 15 days of notification. A separate emergency interim application (référé) is available to suspend a wrongful rejection pending final determination.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or PO box is not acceptable for a French SARL. The company must have a physical French siège social address. The business may lawfully use an authorized domiciliation company (société de domiciliation agréée) under a written and renewable domiciliation contract, and such an arrangement is acceptable for the luxury resale industry provided the address is stated in the statutes, recorded in the RCS, and subject to a demonstrable physical administration capability.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 60% likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection by DGCCRF or French Customs within the first 12 months of operations, increasing to approximately 85% if high-value vintage luxury goods are held in third-party logistics facilities or if the company makes authentication and warranty claims to consumers.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French law firm (Avocat au barreau de Paris or equivalent)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Approved domiciliation company annual contract for registered office

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), Book II, Title II: Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée), Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10, and implementing RCS rules under Articles R.123-1 et seq.; Decree No. 2007-431 on the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce via Guichet Unique Électronique des Formalités des Entreprises (available at guichet-entreprises.gouv.fr), with INSEE issuing SIREN/SIRET identification and DGFIP handling tax registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Business incorporation declaration (Form M0 / Dossier de création d'entreprise) together with signed statutes, publication certificate, capital deposit certificate, and beneficial-owner declaration submitted through the sole electronic window.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for a French SARL (Art. L.223-2 Code de commerce). The articles set the capital. Cash contributions must be fully subscribed and at least 20% paid up at incorporation; the balance must be paid within 5 years. Contributions must be deposited into a blocked bank account or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations before filing and are released only after registration. In-kind contributions are transferred immediately and must be valued in the articles or by a statutory auditor if value exceeds EUR 30,000.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS ADOPTED BY THE FOUNDING MEMBERS ON FORMATION. RESOLVED: That the capital of 10,000 EUR be and it is hereby subscribed in full and reserved in a blocked account, as certified by the depositary. RESOLVED: That the registered office be established at [address], France, as set out in the Articles; that all mail and notices be received there; and that the office may be transferred by decision of the manager. RESOLVED: That [Name] be and is hereby appointed as first gérant (managing officer), with sole authority to operate the company and to open payment and escrow accounts. RESOLVED: That all incorporation formalities be completed and the company be registered in the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-formation name and mark availability verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI trademark register and RCS/Infogreffe corporate-name database via data.inpi.fr and infogreffe.fr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a conflict search on the French trademark register, corporate names, and domain names. No official name reservation is required in France. Select a distinctive corporate name and verify that the corresponding domain and relevant social-media handles are available.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a third party holds a conflicting distinctive sign, amend the proposed name before formal filing; no registry fee is incurred at this stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and signing of articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders and, if real property is contributed, a French notaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the French-language statuts containing legal form, corporate name, registered office address, corporate object limited to online consignment and resale of vintage luxury goods (ISIC 4791), duration of 99 years, share capital, contribution schedule, shareholder identities, manager (gérant) powers, and decision-making rules. Ensure all shareholders sign the final version, either physically or by qualified electronic signature.
required_dossiers: Manager identity and residential address proof
Power of attorney if signatories act by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry reviewers identify a missing or invalid statutory clause, amend and re-sign the statutes before the deposit step; a notarial deed is compulsory only for gifts or real property in-kind contributions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of share capital with a depositary institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French licensed bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a non-interest-bearing account in the name of the company in formation. Deposit the cash portion of the share capital. Obtain a capital deposit certificate (attestation de blocage de fonds) from the depositary. In-kind contributions are identified in the statutes and are deemed delivered upon registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the blocked account for AML reasons, provide traceable source-of-funds evidence or transfer the deposit to another bank or the CDC; the certificate must be reissued accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal notice in a journal d'annonces légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized in the département of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a mandatory legal notice in an authorized legal gazette. The notice must state the proposed company form, founding shareholders, corporate name, registered office, capital, corporate object, duration, and first manager. Obtain the attestation de parution issued by the gazette.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice contains an inaccurate clause, publish a corrective notice in the same JAL and obtain a revised attestation before filing the full dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the incorporation dossier to the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Entreprises (single electronic filing window) transmitting to the Greffe du Tribunal de commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to guichet-entreprises.gouv.fr, complete the business-creation declaration, and upload the required documents. Verify the legal form, corporate object, registered office, managers, and beneficial-owner information. Pay the registry fee and INPI tax electronically. The platform transmits the dossier to the competent commercial registry for examination.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of shareholders and manager
Proof of registered office (lease, rental agreement, or domiciliation agreement)
Power of attorney if an agent files the dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a request for missing parts, upload the required supplementary documents through the same Guichet Unique within the prescribed deadline (generally 15 days or 30 days as stated in the query). If the dossier cannot be cured, file a corrected new application after incorporating the registry observations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration, Kbis extract, and automatic tax/social notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce, INSEE, DGFIP, and URSSAF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon validation of the dossier, the registry issues the Kbis extract certifying the existence and legal capacity of the SARL. INSEE allocates the SIREN and SIRET numbers; DGFIP establishes the fiscal profile; URSSAF is notified for social security affiliation. Review the Kbis carefully for spelling, capital, manager, and office details.
required_dossiers: No additional documents required; dossier submitted at step 5
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis contains errors or registration is delayed, file an observation or rectification request with the greffe through Guichet Unique; provide evidence of the correct data and request immediate reissue.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board applies to an online luxury resale activity without manufacturing, warehousing, or public-access retail premises. The company must remain registered with the RCS and, where applicable, the local mairie may exercise building and civil-defence powers over the registered office.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No prior operating or manufacturing permit is required. As a trader in second-hand movable goods, the company must nevertheless hold and maintain a police register (registre de police) recording high-value acquisitions and sales to comply with traceability and anti-theft obligations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable for a purely digital resale operation; if a physical logistics or storage facility is later opened, DREAL and ADEME will have jurisdiction under the ICPE and extended-producer-responsibility (REP) regimes.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no production, transformation, or treatment operation; no EIA or IPPC/IED permit is triggered by the registered activity at incorporation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions are generated by the e-commerce resale activity. Any sanitary discharge from office space must meet municipal sewer standards; packaging waste generated by shipping must be recycled under French REP schemes and display the Triman logo where required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a pure online activity without public physical access. If a commercial office or warehouse is leased, install fire extinguishers and first-aid equipment in accordance with the French Labour Code, verify electrical installations, keep a building safety log, and conduct an occupational risk assessment. No ERP (établissement recevant du public) occupancy permit is required unless customers physically visit the premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — impots.gouv.fr; corporate formation and tax ID filings via the single business formalities portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); non-resident VAT registration handled by the DGFiP's Service des Impôts des Entreprises through the NOVA e-procedure
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the SARL with the Centre de Formalités des Entreprises (CFE) through the single portal to obtain SIREN, SIRET, APE code, and RCS/Kbis registration; the CFE automatically transmits VAT registration data to the DGFiP, which issues the TVA intracommunautaire (FR VAT ID). Step 2: For a foreign parent or foreign individual shareholders, provide notarized statutes, identity documents, and proof of good standing; non-resident ownership is permitted without restriction, but the SARL must appoint a local legal representative for tax filings and a compliance officer for banking AML purposes. Step 3: For intra-EU distance sales of vintage luxury goods, register in the French OSS portal (guichet unique TVA) to declare and pay destination-country VAT; for imported goods consignments up to EUR 150, use the IOSS scheme. Step 4: The DGFiP issues the SIREN/TVA intracommunautaire dossier within 5–15 working days of electronic filing; a positive Kbis extract is the operative VAT-registration certificate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Default SARL taxation is at entity level under Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS): 25% standard rate, with a reduced 15% rate applied to the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for qualifying small enterprises (Article 219 CGI). An election under Article 206(3) CGI permits pass-through taxation (régime des sociétés de personnes) for a maximum fixed period of five years when all shareholders are natural persons and the conditions of Article 239 bis AA are met; reversion to IS is then mandatory. No US-style check-the-box election exists in France; hybrid mismatch outcomes are neutralized under the ATAD implementing rules of Article 212 bis CGI. The SARL may also join the French VAT group regime (assujetti unique) available since 1 January 2023 for financially, economically, and organizationally linked French taxable persons.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,000 annual taxable turnover for supply of goods (franchise en base de TVA, Article 293 B CGI); once the threshold is exceeded, the SARL must register for VAT from its first taxable transaction. There is no threshold for non-established foreign sellers — VAT registration applies at the first euro of French taxable supplies unless the OSS or IOSS special schemes are used. The intra-EU cross-border distance-sales threshold is EUR 10,000 in annual EU distance sales, above which OSS declaration becomes mandatory for deliveries to other Member States.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing a mandatory e-invoicing/e-reporting reform under the 2022 Finance Act (Article 32) and the Order of 20 July 2022. The rollout was postponed by successive Finance Acts and, as currently projected, applies from September 2026–2028: B2B invoices must be transmitted in the Factur-X (EN16931) structured format through a certified Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) that clears mandated invoice fields to the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF); B2C transactions (including online marketplace sales) require automated e-reporting to the PPF of transaction data, VAT registration IDs, and turnover figures. France does not operate a real-time per-invoice digital-stamping clearance, but invoices must carry one of the recognized anti-fraud quality seals under Article 289 CGI (encrypted hash, PPF routing, or trusted timestamp) to preserve deductibility and probative value in DGFiP audits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: True zero-rating (exemption with input-VAT recovery) is available under Article 262(I) CGI for sales of vintage luxury goods physically delivered from France to a destination outside the European Union, provided the goods are exported by the vendor, by a non-established buyer, or by a carrier on the vendor's behalf, and the exporter holds the prescribed evidence of export by the time the VAT return is filed. Ancillary services directly sold in connection with the export goods (restoration, polishing, authentication tied to the exported item, packing, transport) are likewise zero-rated under Article 262(II) CGI if rendered to the non-EU party and directly related to the exported goods. Intra-EU distance-sales deliveries remain taxable under the destination rules (declarable via OSS), while eligible second-hand/consignment sales may be subjected to the margin scheme (Article 297 A CGI) which taxes only the sale margin and requires specific invoice mentions for each vintage item sold on consignment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EX-E/export summary declaration lodged in DELTA-X) with the Export Accompanying Document (EAD) evidencing the external export procedure
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or signed consignee commercial delivery note proving physical movement from France to the non-EU destination
Commercial Invoice annotated 'TVA non applicable — exportation hors UE / 0% export VAT'
Proof of payment or the inward remittance certificate (or equivalent bank/FX statement from the credit institution or Banque de France)
Source acquisition invoices (unit cost and margin-scheme eligibility records) documenting the input-VAT recovery basis
Appraisal/authentication certificates for vintage-luxury items retained for customs valuation and anti-fraud evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The export zero-rating is denied if the documentary bundle is incomplete, late, or non-compliant; DGFiP may retrospectively claw back the uncollected 20% output VAT together with late-payment interest (intérêts de retard, 0.2% per month capped at 10%) and graduated penalties of up to 40% for material non-disclosure (manquement délibéré) or 80% for dissimulation (Articles 1728 and 1730 CGI). False export documentation or fictitious Customs declarations constitute tax fraud under Article 1741 CGI (up to EUR 500,000 fine and five years' imprisonment) and customs contraventions under the Code des douanes (up to twice the value of the goods plus seizure/confiscation of the exported luxury items). Export VAT refunds are additionally subject to enhanced documentary scrutiny where the consignee is located in a high-risk non-cooperative jurisdiction or where the vintage-luxury unit value exceeds EUR 10,000.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, within the Eurosystem under the monetary authority of the European Central Bank; payment and electronic-money institutions are supervised principally by the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro, which is freely convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions within the European Union and the euro area. France has no general exchange-control regime requiring prior approval for ordinary import payments, export receipts, capital contributions, dividend payments, loan repayments, or transfers to non-residents. Banks may require transaction evidence, beneficial-owner information, source-of-funds evidence, customs or commercial documentation, and payment-purpose information under anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, sanctions, tax-reporting, and statistical-reporting rules. Profit remittances remain subject to French accounting rules, distributable-profit restrictions, corporate income tax, applicable dividend withholding tax, treaty or EU relief, transfer-pricing rules, and bank compliance review. Payments involving sanctioned countries, high-risk jurisdictions, restricted goods, or suspicious trade flows may be delayed, rejected, frozen, or reported.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to the Banque de France or to convert a prescribed percentage of export receipts into euros. No general mandatory conversion ratio or universal statutory repatriation deadline applies to export receipts of a French SARL. Export proceeds may generally remain in euros or foreign currency accounts, subject to the bank's account terms and applicable reporting, sanctions, tax, customs, anti-money-laundering, and accounting obligations. The company should retain contracts, invoices, shipping or delivery evidence, customs records where applicable, payment confirmations, and reconciliation records. Foreign-currency balances must be accounted for under applicable French accounting rules, with exchange differences recognized appropriately.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant Crédit Agricole regional bank
BPCE S.A. and the relevant Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Epargne network bank

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for euro collection, merchant acquiring, foreign-exchange conversion, and international transfers, subject to the provider's risk appetite. An offshore digital EMI cannot lawfully provide regulated payment or electronic-money services to French customers merely because it is accessible online. The provider must be authorized under the applicable national regime and, for EEA services, benefit from valid EU passporting or establish an appropriately authorized French or EEA entity. A non-EEA provider generally requires an applicable French authorization or a regulated EEA partner for regulated services. Account safeguarding, client-money segregation, payment-services disclosures, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, complaint handling, data protection, and safeguarding of funds must be verified. Fintech balances should not be assumed to be bank deposits or covered by the French deposit-guarantee scheme unless the provider and product qualify.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically appear at a bank branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be permitted using qualified or bank-accepted electronic identification, video verification, certified corporate documents, and beneficial-owner verification. The bank may nevertheless require a physical meeting, live video interview, notarized or apostilled documents, a French address, a local signatory, or enhanced verification. For a SARL, the bank will normally identify the company, legal representative, managers, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, business activity, expected transaction profile, counterparties, source of funds, and tax-residency information before activating the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or layered ownership, nominee shareholders, trusts, unexplained holding companies, or inability to identify the ultimate natural-person beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current extract from the French commercial register; articles of association; shareholder register; ownership chart to each natural-person beneficial owner; passports and proof of address for managers, shareholders, and beneficial owners; beneficial-owner filing evidence; board or shareholder authorization; and a written explanation of the ownership and control chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Luxury-goods activity involving high-value goods, cash-intensive transactions, anonymous sellers, consignment arrangements, or rapid turnover inconsistent with the stated business model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan; product categories and price bands; seller onboarding and identity-verification policy; purchase, consignment, and resale agreements; authentication and provenance procedures; sanctions and stolen-goods screening policy; expected monthly transaction volumes; payment-method matrix; refund policy; and sample invoices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border flows involving multiple currencies, high-risk jurisdictions, unusual intermediaries, or payments unrelated to the declared resale activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country and counterparty matrix; expected inbound and outbound flow chart; sample supplier and customer contracts; invoices; shipping and customs documents; import and export records; payment-purpose descriptions; sanctions-screening evidence; tax registrations; and a documented escalation procedure for unusual transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of initial capital, shareholder loans, third-party funding, or capital injections from an account not held by the shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital subscription or shareholder-loan agreement; bank statements; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds narrative; audited or filed financial statements where available; evidence of accumulated business income or sale proceeds; identity of the remitter; and a prohibition or documented explanation for third-party funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between website, registered activity, ISIC classification, merchant-acquiring profile, and actual transaction pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French registration and tax documents; website and platform description; merchant-processing application; operating policies; warehouse or fulfillment evidence; supplier list; marketing materials; inventory model; projected financial statements; and written confirmation that the business does not sell prohibited goods.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete tax-residency information, missing FATCA or CRS self-certification, or inconsistency between management location and declared tax residence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French tax identification information; CRS self-certification; FATCA classification and certification where relevant; tax-residency certificates for relevant entities; management and principal-place-of-business explanation; and confirmation of applicable VAT registrations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, sanctions exposure, politically exposed person status, prior financial-crime concerns, or unexplained account closures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full beneficial-owner and director screening report; legal explanation of any name-match false positive; court or regulatory documents where relevant; compliance policy; independent audit or professional reference; and enhanced-monitoring commitment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route paid-in capital through a French bank or regulated EEA payment institution to the designated capital escrow account in the exact legal name of the SARL. Use the shareholder's own account wherever possible and identify the transfer as paid-in share capital or shareholder funding, not customer revenue. Include the company name, registration details, shareholder identity, capital-subscription reference, and transaction purpose in the payment instructions. Retain the bank transfer confirmation, subscription documents, source-of-funds evidence, and escrow certificate. After incorporation and release of funds, transfer the balance to the operational account only against the bank's corporate-document checklist. For shareholder loans, use a written loan agreement, arm's-length terms, repayment schedule, transfer-pricing analysis where applicable, and accounting entries. France does not impose a universal foreign-exchange purpose-code system equivalent to certain controlled-currency jurisdictions; the bank may nevertheless request an internal purpose code or transaction narrative and may report relevant transactions for regulatory or statistical purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments within the SEPA area where timing and beneficiary requirements permit. Use SWIFT FIN MT103 for supported cross-border customer credit transfers, with ISO 20022 pacs.008 increasingly used as the corresponding modern payment format. Provide accurate ordering-customer, beneficiary, intermediary-bank, invoice, currency, amount, and purpose information. For higher-value or documentary trade transactions, use a commercial documentary letter of credit subject to the agreed rules, commonly UCP 600, with documentary examination and sanctions controls. Use documentary collections under URC 522 where appropriate, or controlled escrow and payment-on-delivery structures for consignment inventory. Match payments to purchase orders, invoices, customs or shipping evidence, and vendor master data. Do not split payments to avoid controls, route funds through unrelated third parties, or use personal accounts. For imports into France, reconcile payment records with customs, VAT, and accounting records; for marketplace or consignment payouts, maintain seller-level ledgers and evidence of seller identity and entitlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts with a regulated bank or authorized investment firm, supported by documented underlying foreign-currency exposure, approved limits, confirmations, valuation, and settlement controls.

Non-deliverable forwards where the relevant currency is non-deliverable or local regulation makes physical settlement impracticable, subject to counterparty authorization, close-out terms, collateral requirements, and sanctions controls.

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps for documented funding or recurring currency exposures, subject to ISDA or equivalent master documentation, legal review, counterparty credit limits, collateral terms, and accounting treatment.
Foreign-exchange spot transactions for operational conversion and liquidity management.
Currency options or collars, where offered by an appropriately regulated counterparty, subject to suitability, premium, scenario, accounting, and board-approved risk limits.

The SARL should prohibit speculative derivatives, maintain a written treasury policy, document the hedged item and hedge purpose, segregate dealing and approval functions, and monitor counterparty, liquidity, valuation, collateral, and termination risks.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Authorities (Direction Générale des Finances Publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of 0.5% of declared turnover per month of delay, capped at 25% of turnover; persistent non-filing may result in administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Audit Report (mandatory if annual turnover exceeds €800,000)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Authorities (Direction Générale des Finances Publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties for late filing of audit report; non-compliance may trigger administrative strike-off

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of UBO information to the RCS; updates required for any shareholding transfers or changes

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A qualifying small company may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profits, subject to turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% individual ownership. The standard 25% rate applies to remaining profits. French tax losses are generally carried forward without a statutory time limit, subject to an annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of current-year taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Carryback is generally limited to the immediately preceding financial year and capped at EUR 1 million.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited under French law, subject to the annual utilization cap; the five-year period is not applicable to ordinary French corporate tax losses

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD for corporate income tax, filed electronically through the French tax administration's professional portal via EDI-TDFC or EFI. Supporting schedules generally include Form 2058-A-SD for tax adjustments, Form 2058-B-SD for tax loss utilization, Form 2058-C-SD for tax credits and carryforwards, Forms 2058-A to 2058-C, and Forms 2059-A to 2059-G for tax balance-sheet and capital-gain information. Form 2572-SD is used for the corporate income tax balance and installment reconciliation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; quarterly or monthly VAT returns may apply separately depending on the VAT regime. Corporate income tax installments are generally payable four times per year, with a final balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the annual corporate income tax return is generally due on the second business day after 1 May of the following year, subject to the electronic filing calendar and any officially granted extension. For a non-calendar year, filing is generally due within three months after year-end. The corporate income tax balance is generally due by the fifteenth day of the fourth month after year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the balance is generally due by 15 May. Installments are generally due by 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, French SIREN number, registered office, fiscal year dates, principal activity, and filing entity classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SARL's own SIREN, registered office, and fiscal year. Foreign shareholder details do not replace the French entity's taxpayer identification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or tax loss after reconciliation of accounting result with French tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the French company's worldwide accounting result as adjusted under French corporate tax rules. Do not report the foreign owner's separate profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary add-backs and deductions, including non-deductible expenses, provisions, depreciation differences, exempt income, and tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only adjustments attributable to the French company. Related-party charges must be supported by agreements, invoices, benefit evidence, and arm's-length analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward, utilized during the year, generated during the year, and remaining after utilization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the EUR 1 million plus 50% excess-profit limitation. Track losses separately where required and retain statutory support for the loss origin.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, tax reductions, and amounts carried forward or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits legally available to the French company and retain certificates, payroll, research, donation, or other eligibility evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax balance-sheet, capital-gain, participation, and tax-accounting information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose French assets, liabilities, shareholdings, capital gains, and tax-accounting movements. Foreign group information is included only where specifically required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax balance, installments paid, withholding credits, tax credits, and amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the balance with the French company's account at the tax administration. Do not offset unrelated foreign tax unless a specific French mechanism permits it.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information concerning qualifying subsidiaries, participation income, tax consolidation, and related tax attributes where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign parent or affiliate relationships where requested and maintain ownership charts, beneficial ownership data, and intercompany agreements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual summary of transactions with associated enterprises, generally required where the applicable transaction category exceeds EUR 100,000, subject to statutory conditions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report cross-border related-party purchases, sales, services, financing, royalties, guarantees, and restructurings using consistent amounts and counterparties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: VAT returns, Forms CA3 or CA12
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: French output VAT, input VAT, intra-Community transactions, imports, and payment or credit position.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For second-hand luxury goods, assess the French margin scheme, ordinary VAT, import VAT, and intra-Community acquisition rules separately. Maintain purchase provenance and margin calculations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing of a corporate tax return generally attracts a 10% penalty, increasing to 40% for a deliberate failure after formal notice and potentially 80% in cases involving fraudulent maneuvering or abusive conduct. Late payment generally attracts interest of 0.20% per month, in addition to applicable penalties. Incorrect returns may attract 40% for deliberate misconduct, 80% for fraudulent maneuvers or abuse of law, and 100% in specified obstruction or concealment situations. Transfer-pricing documentation failures may attract a penalty generally equal to the greater of EUR 10,000 or 0.5% of the transactions lacking required documentation, with additional penalties potentially applying to reassessed profits.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. A qualifying EU or EEA parent may obtain a domestic exemption under the French parent-subsidiary regime, generally requiring at least 10% ownership, a qualifying corporate recipient, a minimum holding period or appropriate undertaking, and anti-abuse compliance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, verify the applicable bilateral tax treaty, recipient tax residence, beneficial ownership, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose-test provisions, minimum holding period, and applicable ownership threshold. Obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's tax authority and retain beneficial-owner and treaty-entitlement evidence. Apply the reduced rate at source only where French administrative requirements are satisfied; otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and seek a refund using the applicable French refund procedure. The payer must report and remit withholding through the French tax administration within the applicable payment deadline and retain evidence supporting the reduced rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic withholding on royalties paid to non-residents is generally 25%, subject to treaty reductions, EU interest-and-royalty relief where all statutory conditions are met, and specific exemptions. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding tax, subject to anti-abuse rules, special regimes, and treaty provisions. Treaty rates vary by recipient jurisdiction and commonly range from 0% to 15% for interest and from 0% to 15% for royalties. The recipient must generally be the beneficial owner and satisfy residence, substance, and anti-abuse requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 150,000,000 annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets generally triggers the full French transfer-pricing documentation obligation under Article L13 AA of the French Tax Procedure Code, subject to statutory ownership and control tests. The threshold is assessed at the French entity or French tax group level as applicable. A transfer-pricing declaration on Form 2257-SD may be required at lower transaction thresholds, generally where a category of transactions with an associated enterprise exceeds EUR 100,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no single general economic substance regulation equivalent to a standalone ESR regime. Substance is assessed through transfer-pricing rules, the beneficial-ownership requirement, the abuse-of-law doctrine, the principal-purpose test in applicable treaties, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, anti-hybrid rules, and general anti-avoidance provisions. A French SARL should maintain genuine local management, decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or credible operational infrastructure, commercial risk assumption, bank-account control, inventory control, and records demonstrating that related-party transactions reflect actual services and arm's-length value.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, understating online marketplace receipts, fabricating purchase costs, claiming non-existent input VAT, manipulating second-hand-goods margin calculations, or concealing beneficial ownership or related-party income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, penalties generally ranging from 10% to 80% and potentially 100% in specified cases. Criminal tax fraud may carry imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, with aggravated cases potentially carrying up to seven years' imprisonment and a fine of up to EUR 3 million, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may incur criminal liability where they personally participated in the offense. A director may also be declared jointly liable for tax debt where fraudulent conduct or serious and repeated non-compliance made recovery from the company impossible. Civil liability generally requires a personal management fault or a fault separable from ordinary corporate functions. Travel restrictions are not automatic; judicial control, bail conditions, asset-freezing measures, or passport restrictions may arise in criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: VAT fraud and carousel or missing-trader arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using fictitious suppliers, false intra-Community acquisitions, circular invoicing, unauthorized margin-scheme claims, concealed import VAT, or knowingly purchasing goods through VAT fraud chains.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, denial of input tax, late-payment interest, penalties up to 80% in fraudulent cases, possible joint and several liability, and criminal prosecution for aggravated fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can face criminal prosecution for intentional participation and civil or tax liability for personal misconduct. Payment service providers, marketplaces, customs records, and bank data may be cross-checked by the tax administration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length management fees, royalties, financing costs, or inventory prices; shifting French resale profits without functional support; or failing to maintain required documentation and Form 2257-SD reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable profit, possible withholding-tax exposure, interest, penalties for inadequate documentation, and a documentation penalty generally equal to the greater of EUR 10,000 or 0.5% of inadequately documented transactions, subject to statutory limits and facts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors generally face corporate liability rather than automatic personal liability, but deliberate falsification, obstruction, fraudulent accounting, or personal participation may create civil or criminal exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, abuse of law, and treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominal French SARL with no genuine activity, local decision-making, inventory control, commercial risk, or beneficial ownership; routing dividends, royalties, or interest through France solely to obtain treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or domestic exemptions, recharacterization of transactions, reassessment, 40% or 80% abuse-of-law penalties depending on the applicable procedure, withholding-tax liabilities, and potential criminal consequences where deception or fraud is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed for knowingly implementing abusive structures, fraudulent declarations, or asset diversion. Corporate separateness is not automatically disregarded; veil-piercing requires legally recognized grounds such as personal fault, fraud, commingling, or an artificial arrangement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-money laundering, terrorist-financing, and beneficial-ownership violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained cash or crypto proceeds, failing to identify consignors or buyers, ignoring suspicious transactions, concealing the ultimate beneficial owner, or failing to maintain required customer and transaction records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative and criminal sanctions may include fines, professional or business restrictions, confiscation, and prosecution under French AML and criminal laws. Obliged professionals may face disciplinary sanctions and reporting failures may aggravate exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and compliance officers may incur personal criminal liability for knowing participation, concealment, or obstruction. Directors may face management bans and imprisonment where the underlying conduct constitutes money laundering or related criminal offenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Counterfeit goods, stolen goods, and provenance failures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling counterfeit luxury goods, knowingly handling stolen goods, falsifying authenticity documentation, or failing to investigate suspicious provenance and serial-number inconsistencies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Confiscation, customs and intellectual-property penalties, damages to rights holders, business closure measures, and criminal penalties. Receiving stolen goods may carry up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine, with aggravated penalties in specified circumstances; counterfeit offenses may carry separate penalties under intellectual-property law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who knowingly sell, import, store, or facilitate counterfeit or stolen goods may be prosecuted personally. Directors may face imprisonment, fines, confiscation, and management restrictions independently of the SARL's civil liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Undervaluing luxury goods, misclassifying goods, concealing commercial imports, using false origin documents, or failing to account for import VAT and duties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of duties and import VAT, customs penalties, seizure or confiscation, and criminal prosecution for serious smuggling or false declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The company and responsible individuals may be liable under customs law. Personal exposure is fact-dependent and may arise from intentional instructions, fraud, or direct involvement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining false accounts, omitting inventory, paying personal expenses from company accounts, distributing unlawful dividends, or transferring assets to related parties without consideration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, civil restitution, shareholder claims, insolvency clawback, criminal accounting offenses, and possible management bans or imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be liable for an insufficiency of assets in insolvency where management faults contributed to the shortfall, and may face personal restitution, asset-freezing, management bans, or imprisonment where criminal conduct is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful dividend distribution and profit repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable profits, bypassing statutory reserves, concealing withholding tax, or paying dividends to a non-beneficial owner without validating treaty relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of unlawful distributions, withholding-tax reassessment, interest and penalties, shareholder or creditor claims, and possible criminal sanctions for misuse of corporate assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be required to restore unlawful distributions and may incur civil or criminal liability for knowingly authorizing distributions contrary to French corporate-law and tax requirements.
